chapter: The Mughal Empire and its Chroniclers
trick: The chronicles are named after their patrons: Akbar Nama by Abul Fazl, Badshah Nama by Lahori for Shah Jahan, Babur Nama by Babur himself in Turkish. The Ain-i-Akbari is the third volume of the Akbar Nama and is the statistical one — provinces, revenue, army. Sulh-i kul, absolute peace, is Akbar's principle of tolerance.

chapter: The Twentieth Century World: Versailles, Holocaust and Bretton Woods
trick: Cause and effect run in a chain here: Versailles 1919 humiliated Germany, the humiliation and the Depression helped bring the Nazis to power, the Nazi state carried out the Holocaust, and after the second war Bretton Woods 1944 built the IMF and the World Bank to prevent the economic collapse that had helped it all along. Learn the chain, not the isolated dates.

trick: Be exact about what these laws were FOR. The Jim Crow laws in the American South and apartheid in South Africa were both designed to ENFORCE racial segregation and keep Black people subordinate — they were not attempts at equality, and 'separate but equal' was the excuse the courts used, struck down in Brown v. Board of Education in 1954. The movements against them are what sought equality.

data.prompt: True or false? Mark each statement about segregation and the movements against it.

items.statement: The Jim Crow laws were intended to enforce the separation of Black and White Americans and to keep Black Americans subordinate.
items.why: They mandated segregated schools, transport and public places, and were paired with devices such as literacy tests and poll taxes to strip away the vote.

items.statement: The Jim Crow laws aimed to place Black and White Americans on an equal footing.
items.why: They did the opposite. The 'separate but equal' formula of Plessy v. Ferguson (1896) was the legal cover, and facilities were never equal.

items.statement: Brown v. Board of Education, 1954, held that segregated schooling was unconstitutional.
items.why: It overturned 'separate but equal' in education and became the legal foundation of the civil rights movement.

items.statement: Apartheid in South Africa was a legally enforced system of racial segregation.
items.why: From 1948 laws classified people by race and controlled where they could live, work, study and travel.

items.statement: Nelson Mandela became South Africa's first Black President in 1994.
items.why: He was released in 1990 after 27 years in prison, and the first non-racial election was held in 1994.

items.statement: Rosa Parks and the Montgomery Bus Boycott belong to the anti-segregation movement.
items.why: Her refusal to give up her seat in 1955 began a boycott of over a year and brought Martin Luther King Jr to national attention.
